# Introduction {-}
We will study the Income data from Chapter 2 of [(ISLR, 2013)](#r2).

# Packages {-}
Packages are ways R uses to let users write their own commands.  They allow R to be open source and gain user involvement with the latest features.

The `devtools` package will be installed, if you have not already done so, and loaded. Then we install and load package `mbadtools` from GitHub. This package is used in USF's MBAD courses and is not on CRAN. The `mbad_standard_packages` object contains a list of required packages for this course that you will need to install first.   
```{r}
# allow package installation from github
if(!("devtools" %in% installed.packages())) install.packages("devtools")
library(devtools) # Make sure that the devtools library is loaded
# install mbadtools from github
if(!("mbadtools" %in% installed.packages())) devtools::install_github("bhartman2/mbadtools")
# load github packages
library(mbadtools)
# list of packages to install
data("mbad_standard_packages")
mbad_standard_packages
# load packages to the notebook
lib_packages(mbad_standard_packages, quiet=TRUE)
```

# Data {-}
Here we get the data using Import Dataset from a csv file Import2.csv.
```{r}
library(readr)
Income <- read_csv("Income2.csv")
```

Display the data to see I got it.
```{r}
Income
```

# Data Description {-}
Describe the data using simple display, or `skim`.
```{r}
Income %>% skim()
```


# Research Problem {-}
We will try to  find out if there is a relationship between `Income` and `Education` level and `Seniority`. 

# Data Wrangling {-}
Make changes to the data for analysis.
```{r}
Income = Income %>% rename(ID = `...1`)
Income %>% glimpse
```

# Data Visualization
Graphic displays of data such as pairs plot.
```{r}
Income %>% select(-ID) %>% 
  ggpairs(progress=F) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title="Pairs Plot of Income Data")
```


# Linear Regression {-}
We run a regression of `Income` on `Education` and `Seniority`.
```{r}
model1 <- lm(Income ~ Education + Seniority, data=Income)
```

See the results:
```{r}
summary(model1)
```

Use modern way.
```{r}
model1 %>% glance
model1 %>% tidy
```

# Conclusion {-}
My conclusions are that `Income` does depend on `Education` and `Seniority` taken together. The linear regression has significant coefficients.
